title: Addressing Multiple Participants: A Museum Robot's Gaze Shapes Visitor Participation

fields.value: Real-world observational field study analyzed using Conversation Analysis.

quotes.text: Using videorecordings from a real-world field study with a museum guide robot, we show procedures by which the robot manages (i) to include and (ii) to disengage users in a multi-party situation.

Analysis of the videorecorded interactions is informed by Conversation Analysis (CA) and investigates the interrelationship between the robot’s and the visitors’ actions and how users interpret the robot’s conduct.

fields.value: The paper analyzes video from a museum field study of a humanoid Nao guide robot whose head orientation shifted toward visitors. In two observed cases, visitors treated those gaze shifts as meaningful: one shift helped bring a visitor into an active group encounter, while another coincided with a visitor disengaging and walking away.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper frames head orientation as gaze and describes its role in including or disengaging visitors, with observed participation effects. It also reports the robot platform and basic gaze implementation.
